html:
SMTO-SSH-0011 — The SSH settings for this computer are broken or have changed

GUID: df0e9dfe-1550-5e31-8def-a7039b0c2e0b
Slug: ssh-configuration-invalid
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • SSH's settings on the Gateway computer either contain a mistake or now send this computer name to a different address, account or port than before. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't send your password or commands to the wrong place.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to run ssh -G with the computer's name and fix any error it reports in the SSH settings file (~/.ssh/config). SSH refuses to connect when its settings file has a typo, an unknown option, or permissions that let other accounts change it.
  2. If the settings were changed on purpose to point to a new address, account or port, continue in a new conversation by typing /new. This conversation remembers the old destination and won't send a password to a different one.
  3. Before running the command again, check whether it already did its job on the remote computer. In some cases SMTO notices the change after the command ran, so repeating it could do the work twice.

What success looks like

  • ssh -G shows the expected address, user and port, and SMTO's SSH command runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't repeat a command whose result you're unsure of until you've checked it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OpenSSH reported an unreadable or invalid client configuration (bad option, missing argument, bad owner or permissions), or ssh -G now resolves a different hostname, user or port than the verified setup, or that check failed or timed out.

What this means

  • Effective SSH configuration lookup fails, exceeds its output bound, or resolves hostname/user/port differently from the retained target setup. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • Effective SSH configuration lookup fails, exceeds its output bound, or resolves hostname/user/port differently from the retained target setup.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate failed configuration resolution from a definite hostname/account/port mismatch.

How to fix it

  • As the Gateway user, run ssh -G for the target and fix errors in ~/.ssh/config (or the -F file), including ownership and permissions (owned by that user, chmod 600). _check_config in src/gateway_core/ssh_privilege.py requires the ssh -G hostname, user and port to equal the verified setup before delivering a password; if the mapping changed on purpose, re-enroll the target from a new conversation. Do not retry an operation whose effect is unknown.
  • Refresh the SSH working context and inspect its effective configuration before requesting a new operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh verified context and effective SSH routing agree before any credential is delivered.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
